key_insight: A decomposed, modality-specific LLM pipeline extracted structured neuroimaging data with high reproducibility and accuracy across three models.
clinical_relevance: The pipeline could support reusable research datasets from emergency dizziness and vertigo imaging reports, with field-specific review rather than autonomous clinical decision-making.
method: Extracted 22 variables across CT head, CT angiography, CT perfusion, and brain MRI; 11 were primary outcomes.
Applied a frozen, temperature-0 pipeline to 1,669 emergency department encounters.
Tested repeatability, nine-week stability, cross-model agreement, and accuracy against an adjudicated reference.
evidence_signal: Independent validation in 200 encounters found pooled primary-variable accuracy of 97.1–98.8%; test–retest exact agreement was 99.8%.
watch_item: Results for rare-finding-enriched encounters measure agreement on model-flagged findings, not sensitivity; field-specific error review remains important.
paper_title: A Reproducible Decomposed Large Language Model Pipeline for Structured Abstraction of Multimodal Neuroimaging Reports: Development and Independent Validation in 1,669 Emergency Department Encounters for Dizziness and Vertigo
